html:
SMTO-MEM-0036 — Knowledge search isn't available right now

GUID: f5251fe6-e0af-59ce-9e41-da68ecd08a5e
Slug: knowledge-rag-unavailable
Domain: MEM · Subsystem: knowledge

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't reach its Knowledge search for this request, so it couldn't look in your documents. Your documents themselves weren't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open System Health and select Check Knowledge. This shows whether Knowledge is running on the server and points to the specific problem if it isn't.
  2. If the check passes, ask the Agent your question again, or use Test retrieval in Knowledge to search your documents. SMTO stopped before reading or adding anything, so asking again is safe once Knowledge is available.
  3. If the check fails, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. They can see on the server why Knowledge isn't connected.

What success looks like

  • Check Knowledge passes and the search returns passages from your documents.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO, saying what you were doing when it happened. Don't delete or re-upload your documents; they are not the cause.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Knowledge was requested but no Knowledge service could be found for this context: the task had no server state owner, that owner has no Knowledge store registered, or System Health found no Knowledge store.

What this means

  • The controller cannot provide the requested search service right now. A component check is needed to narrow the cause. The original operation and completed work retain their own recorded outcomes; this diagnostic does not replay them.

Why this can happen

  • The component reported rag_unavailable. This does not establish the outcome of unrelated operations.

How to diagnose it

  • Knowledge’s status checks pass and retrieval responds.
  • Inspect the error reference and the affected component’s current observation before selecting a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • Run Check Knowledge on System Health and read the server log for the request. The capability context lacked _rag_service, a memory store with a hub, or a resolvable native_state_db_path/_memory_store_path, or the hub has no “rag” repository; confirm the server started with its normal state directory and that Knowledge initialized.
  • Open System Health to inspect Knowledge’s installation and vector service checks. Address the reported condition before searching again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Knowledge’s status checks pass and retrieval responds.

How to verify the fix

  • Knowledge’s status checks pass and retrieval responds.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained task data or repeat an operation with an unknown outcome.

Technical notes

  • Status checks do not replay tasks or modify source documents.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
